characters.name: Tino
characters.description: Tino is a good-hearted and humorous Italian-American boy who is thede factoleader and unanimous "neurotic" of the group. He gets through his days and situations by cutting smart, sarcastic and witty remarks (and breaking the fourth wall). When threatened, he can appear to be a bit of a coward, but despite his neurotic and flighty personality, he has proven on many occasions to be resourceful and brave. Alliterative Name:TinoTonitini. Author Avatar: Is based on creator Doug Langdale's experience growing up with a single mother. Awkward Relatable Schoolkid: He's neurotic, geeky, good-natured, and even a little snarky, in a way the average kid can identify with. Butt-Monkey: Is prone to misfortune, from repeatedly getting trampled by sale-hungry crowds to accidentally using glue instead of sunscreen.

characters.name: Lor
characters.description: A naive, somewhat scatterbrained, and tomboyish Scottish-American girl who is the "jock" of the group. Lor is an avid sports player, and she excels at both basketball and soccer. She is frequently caricatured as the "dumb jock," as many of the jokes revolve around her inability to understand things. Lor is frequently tough and borderline insensitive, to the group's chagrin. All Women Love Shoes: Averted, she wears heels in "Dinner Party" and spends most of the evening complaining about them. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: Probably the biggest offender of the four, although Carver and Tino aren't far behind. Bare Midriffs Are Feminine: Although a stereotypical tomboy in most of her outfits, she has one pink shirt that shows her belly button, completing this trope withPink Means Feminine. Brilliant, but Lazy:Downplayed. She's noChild Prodigy, but she's much smarter than she'll admit. At one point her grades were low enough that her father threatened military school. In the same episode, she got online multiplayer working on one of Tino's games. In an hour or two.Lampshadedimmediately afterwards.noteIf it doesn't sound like much of an accomplishment, remember the show came out in 2000.

characters.name: Carver
characters.description: A self-centered and fashion-conscious African-American boy who is of Haitian descent. He is the self-proclaimed "cool guy" of the group and has a strong interest in clothes and fashion (particularly shoes). Although he appreciates spending time with his friends, Carver desperately wants to be one of the cool kids and, ultimately, to become a celebrity. Big Eater: He polishes off a whole pizza by himself while the gang are talking, much to their annoyance. Deadpan Snarker: Has a tendency to make sassy comments. Did I Just Say That Out Loud?: Tends to blurt out outlandish lies that he then feels obligated to follow up on, like saying Chum Bucket were going to dedicate their next concert to the gang. Hero Worship: He worships the cool kids, Chum Bucket and Kyle fromTeen Canyon.

characters.name: Tish
characters.description: An intellectual and bibliophilic Jewish-American girl of Eastern European descent. She is the most considerate of the four, as she frequently points out what is and is not offensive, and cares about people's feelings. Bespectacled Cutie: She's a cute bookish girl with glasses. Beware the Nice Ones: She tends to be rude and moody when she is mad. So better watch out. Brainy Brunette: She's the brown-haired girl of the group and is something of aChild Prodigy. Drama Queen: She has a tendency to overreact.

characters.name: Thompson Oberman
characters.description: Academic Athlete: Sporty and shown to be a member of the school scholastic society in "Brain Envy" Cool Shades: Usually seen wearing sunglasses. Lovable Jock: He's into sports and a totalNice Guywho patiently puts up with Lor's poorly-thought-out attempts to impress him.

characters.name: Dot Cardigan
characters.description: Genki Girl: Rather excitable, particularly when talking about her crush on Tino. Meaningful Name: Often seen wearing polka dotted cardigan sweaters.

characters.name: Tasha
characters.description: Freaky Fashion, Mild Mind: Dresses punk but shown to be reasonably nice.

characters.name: Bluke and Frances
characters.description: Big Fun: Bluke is pretty chubby, and he's very nice. He also apparently likes to do magic tricks. Catchphrase: Frances' is"I like pointy things". Creepy Child: Frances often giggles creepily and is obsessed with "pointy things", although she's harmless. Hidden Depths: Bluke's simplicity allows him to see a simpler solution and/or the bigger picture. The Tao of Bluke showed this off. For the former, he was able to just relax and have fun compared to everybody coming up with complicated answers. The latter came at the end of the episode; thinking Pizza was the best prize compared to the pool table. After all "You can split a pizza five ways, how do you split a pool table?" Cut to the winners of the table fighting over where it's going. The Hyena: Frances has a very creepy giggle.

characters.name: Colby and Brie
characters.description: Dull Surprise: They never,evershow much emotion. Heel Realization: After Brie becomes uncool in 'Uncool World' and becomes on the receiving end of being mocked, she realizes how hurtful it is and decrees that both she and Colby stop doing it once they both become cool again. Jerkass: They like to verbally tear down others for not being as 'cool' as them- they almostmake Bluke crybefore Tino calls them out on it. Not So Above It All: Brie is a fan of "Li'l Muffins", like several uncool kids. Sunglasses at Night: Brie never takes hers off- the sun burns her eyes.

characters.name: Christy and Candy
characters.description: The Ditz: Neither of them are too bright. The Fashionista: They try to make over Lor in the aptly titled episode "Makeover". Know When to Fold 'Em: The end of "Makeover" shows them ditching their efforts to emulate the supermodel lifestyle and showing an interest in rock climbing and other outdoorsy pursuits. Pink Means Feminine: Candy is seen dressed in pink. Those Two Girls: Never seen by themselves.

characters.name: Chloe Montez
characters.description: Born Unlucky: Does not even begin to cover it. Almost every episode, she's mentioned as being involved in some kind ofNoodle Incident. The Ghost: Frequently mentioned but is never actually seen onscreen.

characters.name: Bebe Cahill
characters.description: Kiddie Kid: Appears to be in the same grade as the weekenders but has a childish interest in "Lil Muffins" and talkng animals. No Social Skills: A lack of this gets her kicked out of the movie theater.

characters.name: Pru
characters.description: Alpha Bitch: Only befriends the gang solely to make her friends jealous. Not to mention she treats them badly during their 'friendship'.

characters.name: Ms. Tonitini
characters.description: Adults Are Useless: Very much averted in the course of the show. It's her advice that usually resolves the conflict of the episode. Amicably Divorced: Is this with Tino's dad. They still talk with each other without any bad blood, and Tino's dad is comfortable voicing his insecurities around her. Deadpan Snarker: Tino definitely learned it from her: they often snark at each other over dinner. Good Parents: She and Tino often have conversations with one another over..."dinner"where she advises him on what he should probably do in order to solve that episode's plot, listening to what he says and giving practical advice. Hippie Parents: A downplayed version, but early press materials described her as a "new-age hippie" and she's shown celebrating the equinoxes and solstices as seasonal holidays. Generally speaking she's pretty lenient in how she parents Tino, and the advice she gives him is grounded and aimed at resolving conflict.

characters.name: Dixon
characters.description: Adults Are Useless: Averted; he gets along with the main protagonists better than other adults because he has a daughter close to their age, and they in turn find it easier to open up to him and ask for advice, since he's relating to them on their level and not talking down to or dismissing them just because they're kids. Friend to All Children: Gets along very well with Tino and his friends, to the point where when it looked like Mrs. Tonitini and Dixon would be getting married Tino was all for it. Real Men Can Cook: Shown to be a talented chef.

characters.name: Coach Colson
characters.description: Drill Sergeant Nasty: Has shades of this as the school PE teacher. Running Gag: Usually answers the door in a bathrobe or towel, screaming atgirl scoutsor salespeople to stop bothering him, only to find the main kids.

characters.name: Mr. Higgenbottom
characters.description: Dirty Communist: Implied to be one in "Crushin' Roulette". Prematurely Bald: Doesn't look that old, but he is partially bald.

characters.name: Gloria Duong
characters.description: Longest Pregnancy Ever: Noticeably pregnant, but never gives birth in any seasons. Sore Loser: Her reaction to losing a go-kart race is to accuse the winner of cheating and pester her for a rematch.
